source_text:
Sed quoniam dilectio non tantum in deum nobis imperata est, cum dictum est: diliges dominum deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua, et ex tota mente tua, sed etiam in proximum — nam, diliges, inquit, proximum tuum tamquam te ipsum - nisi autem ista fides congregationem societatemque hominum teneat, in qua fraterna caritas operetur, minus fructuosa est, credimus et in sanctam ecclesiam, utique catholicam.
nam haeretici et schismatici congregationes suas ecclesias uocant. sed haeretici de deo falsa sentiendo ipsam fidem uiolant; schismatici autem discissionibus iniquis a fraterna caritate dissiliunt, quamuis ea credant quae credimus. quapropter nec haeretici pertinent ad ecclesiam catholicam, quoniam diligit deum, nec schismatici, quoniam diligit proximum. et ideo peccatis proximi facile ignoscit, quia sibi precatur ignosci ab illo, qui nos reconciliauit sibi, delens omnia praeterita et ad uitam nouam nos uocans: quam uitam donec perfectam capiamus, sine peccatis esse non possumus; interest tamen qualia sint.
thought_title: Love of God and neighbor binds the church
orientation: Augustine has just finished the faith about God as creator and renewer, and now turns to the article of the creed on the holy catholic church, grounding it in the twofold command of love.
pass_a_gloss: But since love has been commanded to us not only toward God, when it was said: you shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, and from your whole soul, and from your whole mind, but also toward the neighbor — for, he says, you shall love your neighbor as yourself — unless however this faith holds the gathering and fellowship of human beings, in which brotherly love may work, it is less fruitful, we believe also in the holy church, certainly the catholic one. For heretics and schismatics call their gatherings churches. But heretics, by thinking falsely about God, violate the faith itself; schismatics however, by wicked divisions, leap apart from brotherly love, although they believe the things which we believe. Wherefore neither heretics belong to the catholic church, because he loves God, nor schismatics, because he loves the neighbor. And therefore it easily forgives the sins of the neighbor, because it prays that it be forgiven by him, who reconciled us to himself, blotting out all past things and calling us to a new life: which life until we may take hold of it as perfect, we cannot be without sins; it matters however what kind they are.

choices.why: Glossary term for dilectio; keeps the commanded love of God and neighbor distinct from caritas in the same passage.

choices.english: the gathering and fellowship of human beings
choices.why: Literal rendering of the two nouns joined by -que; preserves the social dimension Augustine is arguing for.
rejected: the assembly and society of men
the congregation and society of humans

choices.why: Literal for fraterna caritas; Augustine uses caritas here for love among brothers, distinct from dilectio commanded toward God and neighbor.
The verb dissilio means to leap or spring apart; keeps the violent image of schism breaking fellowship.
The subject is the heretic (singular masculine), not the church; the church is feminine, but the verb diligit is third singular and the context is the individual heretic.
The subject is the schismatic (singular masculine), not the church; keeps the agency on the individual who fails to love.

bible_refs.note: diliges dominum deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua, et ex tota mente tua
diliges proximum tuum tamquam te ipsum

pass_b_english: But since love has been commanded not only toward God, when it was said, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind” (Deuteronomy 6:5), but also toward the neighbor—for he says, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself” (Leviticus 19:18)—unless this faith holds to the gathering and fellowship of human beings, in which brotherly love is at work, it is less fruitful. Therefore we believe also in the holy church, certainly the catholic church.

For heretics and schismatics call their own gatherings churches. But heretics violate the faith itself by thinking falsely about God; schismatics, however, leap apart from brotherly love by wicked divisions, even though they believe the same things we believe. For this reason neither heretics belong to the catholic church, because she loves God, nor do schismatics, because she loves the neighbor. And so she readily forgives the sins of her neighbor, because she prays to be forgiven by him who reconciled us to himself, blotting out all past things and calling us to a new life. Until we lay hold of that life in its perfection, we cannot be without sins; but it matters what kind they are.

problems.why: Subject changed from 'she/it' (ecclesia) to 'he'; heretics don't belong because the church loves God, not because 'he' does.
Subject changed from 'she/it' (ecclesia) to 'he'; schismatics don't belong because the church loves neighbor, not because 'he' does.
problems.ruling: 'quoniam diligit proximum' refers to ecclesia (fem.); 'he loves' misleads reader about agency and argument.

fixed: Changed 'he' to 'it' in 'because he loves God' to match the church as subject (source: 'quoniam diligit deum', with 'ecclesia' as the implied subject).
Changed 'he' to 'it' in 'because he loves the neighbor' to match the church as subject (source: 'quoniam diligit proximum', with 'ecclesia' as the implied subject).

problems.quote: because it loves God, nor schismatics, because it loves the neighbor
problems.source_quote: quoniam diligit deum, nec schismatici, quoniam diligit proximum
problems.why: Subject of 'diligit' is the catholic church, not heretics/schismatics; 'nec' links to neither belonging.
problems.fix: because it loves God, nor do schismatics, because it loves the neighbor
problems.ruling: Source 'diligit' refers to ecclesia catholica (feminine singular), not heretics/schismatics; 'nec' = 'nor' links both exclusions to church's love.

problems.quote: the church readily forgives the sins of the neighbor
problems.source_quote: et ideo peccatis proximi facile ignoscit
problems.why: Subject shift: Latin 'ignoscit' lacks explicit subject but context shows 'fides' or the believer; English 'the church' makes church the agent, but Augustine speaks of the individual forgiving neighbor.
problems.fix: And so one readily forgives the sins of one's neighbor
problems.ruling: 'ignoscit' subject shifts to individual believer, not church; 'the church readily forgives' misleads reader on agency.

problems.quote: because it prays to be forgiven
problems.why: Subject confusion continues: 'it prays' refers to church, but Latin 'sibi precatur' refers to the individual believer praying for themselves to be forgiven.
problems.fix: because one prays to be forgiven for oneself
problems.ruling: 'sibi precatur ignosci' = believer prays for own forgiveness; 'it prays' wrongly assigns to church, changing meaning.

edits.old: neither heretics belong to the catholic church, because it loves God, nor schismatics, because it loves the neighbor.
edits.new: neither heretics belong to the catholic church, because it loves God, nor do schismatics, because it loves the neighbor.

edits.old: And so the church readily forgives the sins of the neighbor, because it prays to be forgiven by him
edits.new: And so one readily forgives the sins of one's neighbor, because one prays to be forgiven by him

fixed: Added 'do' to clarify that 'nec schismatici' continues the negation, matching the source's 'nec schismatici, quoniam diligit proximum'.
Changed 'the church' to 'one' for 'ignoscit' and 'precatur', since the Latin verbs lack an explicit subject and the context points to the individual believer, not the church.

problems.why: Subject changed: 'it' (church) for 'she' or 'one' (faith/person). Latin has no explicit subject; antecedent is faith or believer.
problems.fix: because she loves God, nor do schismatics, because she loves the neighbor

problems.why: Same issue: impersonal 'one' obscures that the subject is the same believer/church member who forgives.

edits.old: neither heretics belong to the catholic church, because it loves God, nor do schismatics, because it loves the neighbor.
edits.new: neither heretics belong to the catholic church, because she loves God, nor do schismatics, because she loves the neighbor.

edits.old: And so one readily forgives the sins of one's neighbor, because one prays to be forgiven
edits.new: And so she readily forgives the sins of her neighbor, because she prays to be forgiven

fixed: Changed 'it' to 'she' in both clauses to restore the personal subject (faith/believer) implied by the Latin 'diligit', matching the suggested fix.
Changed 'one' to 'she' to keep the same personal subject throughout the sentence, matching the suggested fix.

dismissed.why: Subject is 'ecclesia catholica' (the church), not 'she' ambiguously; more critically, 'diligit' is 3rd singular but the logic shows the church is what heretics/schismatics lack: the church loves God and neighbor, which they don't. The English 'she' is okay but the causal logic is inverted: heretics don't belong because the church loves God (which they don't share in). The real problem: 'diligit' refers to the church's love, but the English makes it sound like a reason for exclusion rather than a defining mark of the true church.
dismissed.note: 'She' correctly refers to the catholic church as the subject of 'diligit', and the logic is not inverted.
